profile.summary: scGPT-spatial is a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics, made by continuing the pre-training of the scGPT single-cell model on 30 million spatial profiles. It takes spatial transcriptomic data from imaging or sequencing protocols (Visium, Visium HD, Xenium, MERFISH) and outputs zero-shot cell or spot embeddings for multi-slide and multi-modal integration; the authors report that the model also supports cell-type deconvolution and missing gene imputation.

summary_quotes.text: a specialized foundation model for spatial transcriptomics continually pretrained on our previously published scGPT scRNA-seq foundation model
comprising of 30 million spatial transcriptomic profiles, encompassing both imaging- and sequencing-based protocols
effectively supports cell-type deconvolution and contextualized missing gene expression imputation

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: scGPT-spatial starts from the published scGPT model and continues pre-training on the SpatialHuman30M corpus. It adds a Mixture of Experts decoder that routes each sample to protocol-aware decoding of gene expression, samples training data in a spatially aware way, and uses a neighbourhood-based reconstruction objective to capture which cell states co-locate in tissue. At inference, embed_data returns an embedding per cell or spot.

quotes.text: scGPT-spatial introduces a novel MoE (Mixture of Experts) decoder that adaptively routes samples for protocol-aware decoding of gene expression profiles
employs a spatially-aware sampling strategy and a novel neighborhood-based training objective
You can simply call the `scgpt_spatial.tasks.embed_data()` function below to generate zero-shot embeddings for cells/spots.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One release, scGPT-spatial V1, is on Figshare (article 28356068, version 1) as scGPT_spatial_v1.zip. The archive holds best_model.pt, args.json, vocab.json, batch_mapping_dict.json and all_dict_mean_std.csv, and the tutorial says all of these must sit in the checkpoint folder. A result should name V1 and the repository commit.

quotes.text: Make sure all the downloaded `.json` and `.csv` files are also in the checkpoint folder - not just model weights!

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Zero-shot embedding of spatial data for integration across slides and protocols. The authors report that the model also supports cell-type deconvolution and missing gene imputation; the sources read do not say whether these use the embeddings. Only the zero-shot integration tutorial is released; the README says more code is coming.

run_guide.summary: Clone the repository, download the V1 weights archive and compute zero-shot embeddings for an AnnData with the tutorial's embed_data call.
prerequisites: A Python environment set up following the scGPT repository's instructions (not reviewed here).
The scGPT_spatial_v1.zip archive from Figshare, unpacked with all .json and .csv files kept beside best_model.pt.
An AnnData of spatial profiles with a gene name column.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/bowang-lab/scGPT-spatial
cd scGPT-spatial
git checkout --detach f9442d777ba47cd3dcac8253833a233ff5bf7262
steps.explanation: The README's clone command; the checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit.

steps.title: Download the weights
steps.shell: # Download scGPT_spatial_v1.zip from https://figshare.com/articles/software/scGPT-spatial_V1_Model_Weights/28356068 and unpack it to checkpoints/scGPT_spatial_v1
steps.explanation: The README gives only a Figshare link; the tutorial reads the checkpoint from ../checkpoints/scGPT_spatial_v1 relative to the tutorials folder.

steps.title: Embed cells or spots
steps.shell:
cd tutorials
python - <<'EOF'
import sys
import scanpy as sc
sys.path.insert(0, "../")
import scgpt_spatial

adata = sc.read_h5ad('../data/processed_fetal_lung_visium_xenium.h5ad')
model_dir = '../checkpoints/scGPT_spatial_v1'
gene_col = 'feature_name'
cell_type_col = 'celltype'
ref_embed_adata = scgpt_spatial.tasks.embed_data(
    adata,
    model_dir,
    gene_col=gene_col,
    obs_to_save=cell_type_col, 
    batch_size=64,
    return_new_adata=True,
)
EOF
steps.explanation: Lines from the tutorial notebook, wrapped in a shell heredoc by Rewire and run from the tutorials folder. The demo data file is not in the repository; substitute your own AnnData and gene column.

outputs: ref_embed_adata: a new AnnData whose X holds one zero-shot embedding per cell or spot, with the cell type column carried over.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The environment depends on scGPT's install instructions, not reviewed here.
The tutorial's demo dataset is not shipped in the repository.

notes: The preprint's only open copy found is on bioRxiv: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.02.05.636714v1 (PDF not requested). The Europe PMC record gives the abstract licence as cc by-nc-nd. The Figshare record is at version 1, so its published date is taken as the release date.
